entries.title: British English: Is ‘Thorough’ Really Praise?
entries.hook: Your manager says your report is ‘certainly thorough.’ Is that praise?

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: Well, it’s certainly thorough. Could we produce a two-page version for the board?

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: The request for a shorter version shows that thorough also means too long for this audience.

entries.prompt: What action reveals the implied meaning?
entries.answer: The request for a two-page version.
entries.visualBrief: Bright polished anime boardroom with one adult professional holding a very thick report beside a slim abstract summary, hands hidden behind documents, teal gold and navy, no readable text.

entries.title: Stop Taking a Late Reply Personally
entries.hook: A late reply is a fact. Rejection is a story until you verify it.

turns.speaker: mia
turns.text: I sent the draft Monday. It is Tuesday evening, and there is no reply.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: That is the fact. ‘My work was rejected’ is one possible interpretation, not confirmed evidence.

turns.speaker: mia
turns.text: I’ll send one follow-up with my Thursday deadline.

entries.prompt: What is the next useful action?
entries.answer: Send a factual follow-up with the deadline.
entries.visualBrief: Warm expressive anime home-office scene with an adult woman calmly reviewing an unanswered laptop message, shoulders-up, hands below desk, rust blue and cream, no readable text.

entries.title: Take It with a Pinch of Salt
entries.hook: A colleague says, ‘Take that rumour with a pinch of salt.’ What should you do?

turns.speaker: mia
turns.text: I heard the company is closing the Bristol office.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: I’d take that with a pinch of salt. The same source shared a false rumour last month.

turns.speaker: mia
turns.text: I’ll wait for the official staff meeting.

entries.prompt: Believe it, ignore all news, or stay sceptical?
entries.answer: Stay sceptical and wait for reliable information.
entries.visualBrief: Lively bright anime office with two adult colleagues discussing a rumour, one abstract speech bubble fading beside an official notice shape, hands out of frame, blue coral and cream, no readable text.

entries.title: One Delay or a Pattern?
entries.hook: One late arrival and ten late arrivals are not the same evidence.

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: A friend was late once because a bus broke down. Patience made sense.

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: Then the friend arrived forty minutes late every week and never sent an update.

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: The useful response changed: name the repeated impact and set a clear limit.

entries.prompt: What three things should you check?
entries.answer: Pattern, impact, and whether the person repairs the problem.
entries.visualBrief: Bright anime split scene with the same adult waiting once calmly and later noticing a repeated calendar pattern, shoulders-up, hands hidden, warm yellow navy and coral, no readable text.
